text: Albania's revised 2027 fiscal package drops a corporate‑tax increase and introduces lower VAT on basic foods, higher standard VAT, a new 30% top‑income tax rate and a lower turnover threshold for VAT registration, the government says. Opposition leaders, including Sali Berisha and Ervin Salianji, denounce the measures as harmful to businesses, while Prime Minister Edi Rama defended them on X as a fair redistribution of growth benefits.

sources.title: Albania’s 2027 Fiscal Package Sparks Backlash Over Higher Taxes and Investment Risks - Tirana Times
sources.articleText:
The American Chamber of Commerce warns of risks to foreign investment as the government’s 2027 fiscal package faces growing opposition from businesses, lawmakers and economists.
TIRANA, Albania , Oct. 29 – Albania’s government has unveiled a controversial 2027 fiscal package, proposing significant changes to value-added tax, dividend taxation, personal income taxes, and small-business obligations. Prime Minister Edi Rama has presented the measures on October 28 as an effort to redistribute the benefits of economic growth, but business organizations and opposition parties have strongly criticized the proposals, warning of higher prices, weaker competitiveness, and declining investment.
